title: AI System Design: From Idea to Production - Apoorva Joshi, MongoDB
talk_summary: A MongoDB developer advocate walks through a four-phase framework (product requirements, system design, evaluation/monitoring, optimization) applied to a hypothetical health-insurance claims review system.

takeaways.technique: Define guardrail-compliance and quality metrics before shipping, then monitor the same metrics plus implicit signals in production
takeaways.what_they_do: They enumerate concrete metrics per layer: input guardrail rejection rate, output missing-citation rate, faithfulness to retrieved sources, a domain North-Star metric, and system cost/token metrics; in production they add implicit signals like human-override rate and time-to-review as regression alarms.

takeaways.technique: Structured outputs that force decision plus citations
takeaways.what_they_do: They require the model to emit a structured object containing not just the verdict but the citations/evidence that justified it, and treat a response lacking citations as invalid via an output guardrail.
takeaways.evidence_quote: structured outputs, which would be a good one to make sure that our system is always producing a structured output which contains not just the decision, but also the citations

takeaways.technique: Start with the simplest control-flow design, evaluate, then add autonomy only where it fails
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of jumping to agents, they map the workflow, pick the minimal pattern (RAG + predetermined control flow + human-in-the-loop), and iterate only on measured gaps; they explicitly warn that letting a coding agent choose architecture yields over-engineering.
takeaways.evidence_quote: start with the simplest design, evaluate it, find gaps during the evaluation, and iterate from there

takeaways.technique: Semantic caching and batch processing for repeated similar work
takeaways.what_they_do: They suggest caching decisions for semantically similar past inputs and batching requests instead of processing one at a time, as cost/latency levers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: semantic caching could be useful to expedite decisions based on uh similar claims from the past

takeaways.technique: Reranking retrieved context before it hits the model
takeaways.what_they_do: They call out reranking as an accuracy lever because ordering retrieved information by relevance matters to LLM output quality.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a reranker will make sure that the information being retrieved um is surfacing information in the right order of relevance

takeaways.technique: Quantified, solution-agnostic problem statement with a time-bound success metric
takeaways.what_they_do: Before design, they require a business problem that names users, current state, and a measurable baseline, plus one or two SMART success metrics, explicitly not prescribing the architecture.
takeaways.evidence_quote: reduce the average processing time for urgent claim review requests from 2 days to 1 hour within 90 days of launch
